newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers mostly steady.

text.p: Basis offers for soymeal in U.S. cash markets were mostly steady Friday with very little trade reported, dealers said.
"Nobody is buying anything right now because nobody wants to buy versus the August (CBOT contract)," said one dealer.
CBOT August soymeal holds a nearly $30.00-per-ton premium to September, so most buyers are content to wait until August expires on August 20.
The National Oilseed Processors Association reported a crush of 24.341 million bushels versus 23.549 million last week.
This week's crush also surpassed trade expectations for 22.7 million to 24.1 million bushels.
"Margins were good last week, so I guess crushers went after it pretty agressively," said one soymeal dealer.
Basis offers at some locations were unquoted because crushers are taking downtime and have no soymeal for sale, they said.
"We're out of the market," said one Indiana crusher. "We have only two truckloads to sell right now."
